audit.title: Create and manage VRF V2.5 subscriptions

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; each section opens with a self-contained imperative ("To create a VRF 2.5 subscription:", "To fund your subscription:"). No "as above" dependencies. Slight weakness: no top-line definition of what a subscription *is*.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Good: 7 headings, 1 H1, max depth H3, 0 level skips, no section over 600 words (max 329). No tables where an actions/parameters table would extract cleanly. MDX `<TabsContent>` tabs may flatten or confuse chunkers.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak: 29 numerals but 0 with units and 0 hex identifiers; these are mostly step numbers. No minimum funding amount, no supported-network specifics inline, no subscription-ID format, no gas/token details.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Adequate: 10 links (6 internal, 4 external), including the Remix sample contract and Supported Networks page. Claims are attributable to the right hubs.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Weak: no crisp one-sentence definition of "VRF subscription," "consumer," or "native token" balance near first use — nothing an engine can lift verbatim to answer "what is a VRF subscription."

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak (measured): 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, datePublished/dateModified absent, no og/twitter tags. Head metadata could not be verified — the CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full read, but the served HTML shows none.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Weak: 0 fenced code blocks. The programmatic section names Solidity functions and ABI-encoded parameters but shows no copy-pasteable snippet — an agent cannot execute this section as written.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Good lifecycle coverage (create/add/fund/cancel/programmatic) including the contract-admin cancellation edge case, but no symptom- or error-phrased entries and no explicit troubleshooting section.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent naming (VRF V2.5, Subscription Manager, consumer), unambiguous prose. No action needed.

audit.summary: This is a clean, well-structured task guide covering the full VRF V2.5 subscription lifecycle (create → add consumer → fund → cancel), plus a programmatic path. Its biggest strength is action-first section leads with clear numbered steps; its biggest weakness is that the "programmatically" half references functions (`createSubscription`, `transferAndCall`, `topUpSubscription`) but ships **zero fenced code blocks** and no concrete specifics (no minimum LINK amounts, no coordinator addresses, no subscription-ID format), while the page carries no JSON-LD, canonical, or last-updated signal. For a page whose value proposition includes agent-runnable programmatic setup, the missing code and specifics are the primary retrieval/fidelity risk.

recommendations.title: Add runnable Solidity/CLI snippets to the programmatic section
recommendations.where: "Create a subscription programmatically" → both tab panels
recommendations.issue: "Expand the `createSubscription` function and select the **Write** button" — no code shown.
recommendations.change: Add fenced, language-tagged snippets: the `SubscriptionManager.sol` create call, and a `transferAndCall(coordinator, amount, abi.encode(subId))` example with a comment showing how `data(bytes)` is ABI-encoded. Include imports/pragma so it compiles standalone.
recommendations.why: Agents reading this section currently cannot complete the task; complete labeled snippets are directly liftable and are the highest-lift gap here.

recommendations.title: Add a canonical, liftable definition of "VRF subscription" up top
recommendations.issue: Page opens into task steps with no definition of the entity.
recommendations.change: Add one to two sentences: "A VRF V2.5 subscription is an account that funds and authorizes one or more consumer contracts to request randomness, holding both a LINK balance and a native-token balance."
recommendations.why: Gives engines a self-contained answer to "what is a VRF subscription," the query this page should own.

recommendations.title: Add symptom-phrased headings / a short troubleshooting block
recommendations.where: After "Cancel your subscription and withdraw funds"
recommendations.issue: Edge case buried in prose: "If your subscription's admin address is a contract instead of an EOA, you may not be able to cancel…"
recommendations.change: Promote to an H3 phrased as the user's question, e.g. "Can't cancel subscription — admin address is a contract" with the transfer-ownership fix as the first sentence. Add "How much LINK do I need to fund a subscription?" if a minimum exists.
recommendations.why: Devs/agents query by symptom; question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses.

recommendations.title: Add concrete specifics inline
recommendations.issue: 0 numerals with units; no funding minimums, token decimals, or coordinator address example.
recommendations.change: State the two balance types explicitly with token units, any minimum-balance requirement, and link/inline an example coordinator address per network (or clearly point to the exact row on Supported Networks).
recommendations.why: Quantitative specifics are among the highest-lift changes for citation; qualitative-only prose underperforms.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD, canonical URL, and visible last-updated
recommendations.issue: Measured: 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no dateModified.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `dateModified`, add a `<link rel="canonical">`, and surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Freshness and schema raise agent trust/parseability (E-E-A-T); note this is likely a site-template fix, not page-local.

recommendations.title: Add a Subscription Manager actions table
recommendations.change: Add a 3-column table: Action · Where in UI · Result/effect.
recommendations.why: Tables let engines extract discrete reasons/steps and build justified answers.

antiPatterns: MDX components (`<Vrf2_5Common>`, `<TabsContent>`, `<Fragment>`) render as raw tags in the served markdown; tab content may be split or dropped by chunkers — verify the rendered HTML exposes both panels as plain text.
No stale/keyword-stuffing/fluff issues; prose is clean and undated only at the metadata level.
offPageNotes: JSON-LD, canonical, and last-updated are almost certainly controlled by the site template — fix once at the layout level to benefit all VRF pages.
`llms.txt` is already referenced at the top of the page — good; ensure this URL is listed in it.
Consider internal links from the Supported Networks and VRF landing pages into this page under the canonical-hub pattern to defend against sibling pages being outranked.
